_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::input_format#28. `4C --parameters 2>/dev/null` exits 0 and emits 2 926 432 bytes of YAML starting 'metadata:' / 'commit_hash: 89519cfe...' / 'version: 2026.2.0-dev', with exactly seven top-level keys in this order: metadata, legacy_element_specs, legacy_particle_specs, cell_types, sections, $references, legacy_string_sections. It declares 478 input sections and 60 legacy element names on this build, and carries 11980 'required:' flags, one per parameter. Capturing with 2>&1 instead adds 30 bytes of local X11 warning on this host, so any size or hash must redirect stdout alone — only the direction (2>&1 can only be larger) is asserted, since how much host noise there is varies. The last two arms show why the dump is the right thing to consult: 'STRUCTURAL DYNAMIC' is present (1) and the near-miss 'STRUCTURAL DYNAMICS' is absent (0), and feeding that absent name to the same binary gives "Section 'STRUCTURAL DYNAMICS' is not a valid section name." and exit 1. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: TOP_LEVEL_KEY_LIST=metadata legacy_element_specs legacy_particle_specs cell_types sections $references legacy_string_sections
Section 'STRUCTURAL DYNAMICS' is not a valid section name.

_mutation.note: take the dump with 2>&1 as most people would. On this host that adds 30 bytes of X11 warning, CLEAN_BYTES stops being 2926432, and the fixture must go red — which is exactly the mistake the entry warns about.
stop consulting the dump and write the invented section anyway: name a section that does exist, so the not-a-valid-section diagnostic vanishes and the fixture must go red.
